research_rationale: EO 10468 (signed 1953-07-07 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1953-07-07, 4:09 p.m.; 18 FR 3979, Federal Register of July 9, 1953 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10468.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative paragraph and one closing sentence. The paragraph appoints William C. Strand, Director, Office of Territories, Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, vice James P. Davis, resigned, to serve without additional compensation and to exercise and discharge the functions, duties and authority that Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 conferred on the Administration and its Administrator. The closing sentence amends those orders accordingly. There is no deadline, sunset or condition. First end: both commands are one-time acts. The appointment was made, and the amendments to the earlier orders took effect, when the order was signed; the text has no effective-date wording, so the signing date 1953-07-07 is recorded (the filing date is the same day). What survives is a consequence of the performed appointment and not a continuing command of this order: Strand's holding of the office and the earlier orders as amended. The functions he exercises come from Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689, not from this order. No held source shows when Strand left the office or when the Administration ended. A contents line in the held Federal Register text printed with EO 10597 (issue of 1955-02-17) lists an Interior Department notice on cessation of functions and activities of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration at 20 FR 1027; the notice itself is not held. Those facts concern the surviving appointment and the earlier orders, not whether this order's own commands were performed. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10468 found only the order's own copies and a page number in another document; a scan of held order texts numbered above 10468 for the Administration's name and for Strand's name found no order. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search, which found no hit for the appointee.
savings_reason: The appointment of Strand and the amendments to Executive Orders 7057, 7180, 7554 and 7689 are performed acts whose consequences continue independently of any command left in this order: the appointment stands as the act that placed Strand in the office until his service ended, and the earlier orders stand as amended. The order contains no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. The end of Strand's service and of the Administration is not shown by a held source and is not needed to fix when this order's own commands were performed.

savings_check: Surviving consequence stated as continuing_independent: the performed appointment and the amended earlier orders. No held source fixes the end of Strand's service or of the Administration.

research_rationale: EO 10569 (signed 1954-10-05 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-10-07, 10:12 a.m.; 19 FR 6493, Federal Register of October 8, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10569.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier inventory lists eleven clauses, but ten of them are Civil Service Commission notices printed after the order on the same Federal Register page (subsections (k), (b) and (e) of the exceptions from the competitive service) and are not part of this order. I replace the inventory with one clause, characters 1180 to 1563 of the registered file: the sentence that amends Executive Order 10334 of March 26, 1952, which exempted Frederick C. Mayer, organist and choirmaster at the United States Military Academy, from compulsory retirement for an indefinite period, by substituting the words until December 31, 1954 for the words for an indefinite period of time in its last paragraph, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932. The two recitals command nothing. First end: the amended exemption runs until December 31, 1954. Following the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates, the end is recorded as that stated date, inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 31, 1954); the exclusive reading is the alternative, under which the exemption ends when December 31, 1954 begins. The amending act itself was performed when the order took effect; the lifecycle of this order is the period it fixed for the exemption. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10569 found only the order's own copies and unrelated page numbers; a scan for the appointee's name found Executive Order 10334, the recitals of this order, and no later order extending or renewing the exemption; the person-name machine search found no hit. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts). I also adopted the held-text person-name search.
savings_reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. After December 31, 1954 the exemption it fixed no longer applies, and nothing in the order preserves any effect past that date; Executive Order 10334 is a separate order whose own exemption the amendment limited.
earlier_end_check: Nothing held amends, revokes or shortens the order or the amended exemption before December 31, 1954. The appointee could have left service earlier, but no held source says so and the stated date is the order's own end.
scope_check: One clause after correcting the dossier inventory, which had added ten neighboring Civil Service Commission notices to the order. The amended exemption is not partial.
independent_command_check: The only command is the amendment, which sets the end of the exemption; the effective-date wording of the neighboring notices does not belong to this order.
savings_check: None stated; after the end date no exemption continues.

research_rationale: EO 10580 (signed 1954-12-04 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-12-06, 11:32 a.m.; 19 FR 8037, Federal Register of December 7, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10580.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one operative sentence with two joined commands limited to two days. First, the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia, including the General Accounting Office, the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Naval Stations, are closed all day on Friday, December 24, 1954 and one-half day on Friday, December 31, 1954. Second, federal employees in that area and in the field service, except those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law, are excused from duty on that day and that half day, each of which is a holiday within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. There is no recital, report deadline, extension or renewal. First end: by its own terms the order operates only on those two days, so it was fully performed at the close of December 31, 1954; the December 24 closing was spent earlier. The text has no until-wording, so the end is the last stated day. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8); it cannot end this order, and the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10580 found no order text that names it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).
savings_reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. Pay and leave for the excused day and half day follow the compensation and leave statutes and Executive Order 10358, which the order invokes but does not extend, so nothing keeps the order operative after December 31, 1954.
earlier_end_check: Nothing held amends, extends or revokes the order before the stated days; each day ends at its close by the order's own terms. EO 10358 is an earlier order and does not reach it.
scope_check: One clause covering one full day and one half day; no partial amendment or partial end is held or found.
independent_command_check: The closing and the excusal are one command for the same two days; the holiday designation invokes EO 10358 and statutes and does not run past the days.
savings_check: None stated. Pay and leave for the excused day and half day depend on statute and EO 10358 and do not keep this order operative.
